chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from his brother Ja'far ibn Isa ibn Yaqteen, from Abu al-Hasan al-Awwal (peace be upon him), who said:

There is no problem with the testimony upon the confession of the woman, and she is not required to uncover her face, if she is recognized by her eyes, or if someone who recognizes her is present. But if she is not recognized by her eyes, and no one who recognizes her is present, then it is not permissible for the witnesses to testify upon her and upon her confession unless she uncovers her face and they look at her.
ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for a woman's testimony if her face is covered?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the jurisprudential balance between preserving a woman's modesty (haya) and ensuring legal validity in testimony, a key concern in Shia fiqh. It establishes that visual identification of the face is not strictly mandatory if the witness knows the woman personally or can identify her by her eyes, thereby preventing unnecessary exposure. However, in cases of unfamiliarity, the witnesses must see her face uncovered to validate the confession, highlighting the practical application of 'uncovering' (ifsar) in legal contexts.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from his brother Ja’far Bin Isa Bin Yaqteen, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> the 1<sup>st</sup> having said:

‘There is no problem with the testimony upon the confession of the woman, and it is not with an uncovered face, when she is recognised by her eyes, or there is present someone who recognises her. So if she cannot be recognised by her eyes, and there is none present who recognises her, so it is not allowable for the witnesses that they should testify upon her, and upon her confession, besides if she is covered and one looks at her (for identification)’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from his brother Ja‘far ibn ‘Isa ibn Yaqtin who has narrated the following: “Abu al-Hassan, al-Awwal, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has pronounced this fatwa.

’Bearing testimony to the confession of a woman, whose face is not open, if one knows her in person or the one who is present knows her, is not harmful. However, if she is not known in person and no one present knows her, then bearing testimony against her or against her confession is not permissible without her face being uncovered so that he can look at her face/”
